headline: Council approves Ethical Purchasing Ordinance on companies in Israel and Palestine, 10-1, and a $410,037 warming center grant.
summary: The council amended short-term rental rules to close loopholes. It set the residential tax factor at 84.15 and a 35% residential exemption. It also sent an accessory dwelling unit change back to committee and approved money for street reconstruction.
decisions: Approved the short-term rental ordinance amendment and ordained it, with 11 members in favor.
Approved the Ethical Purchasing Ordinance by a 10-1 vote and ordained it.
Approved Eversource conduit work on Morland Street to serve 16-18 Morland Street.
Approved Eversource conduit work on Clark Street to serve 26 Clark Street.
Approved Eversource conduit work on Prospect Avenue, tied to the Webster Avenue bridge project.
Approved the minimum residential factor of 84.15 and a 35% residential exemption for fiscal year 2027.
Referred the Block 9, Assembly Square housing tax increment financing agreement to the Finance Committee.
Sent the accessory dwelling unit zoning amendment, item 26-1336, back to the Land Use Committee.
Approved $2,383,850 in parking meter receipts to lower the fiscal 2027 tax rate.
Approved $46,270 from the tax levy for an update to the hazard mitigation plan.
Approved $140,831 for street reconstruction from the pay-as-you-go capital account.
Approved accepting and spending a $410,037 state grant for the 2026-2027 Winter Warming Center.
Approved about $319,694 in city transfers and appropriations to cover the Winter Warming Center's operating costs, by roll call.
Approved an exception to let Secured Environments Pest and Wildlife Services use air rifle rodent control in Ward 7.
Approved a resolution asking the Director of Mobility to work with the council on an Emergency Streets Protocol, with the Office of Emergency Management added.
Approved a resolution asking the Director of Finance to begin tracking city purchases of artificial intelligence products.
Approved suspending the rules to move the annual caucus to December 10, 2026.
Referred the ordinance to repeal the medical panel for firefighters and police officers to the Legislative Matters Committee.
Referred a list of mayor's requests, items 7.7 through 7.30, to the Finance Committee.
discussion: Ethical Purchasing Ordinance: Supporters cited Ballot Question 3 and the rights of Palestinians. Opponents said the ordinance could make Jewish residents feel targeted and raised legal concerns.
Tax classification and rate: Discussion covered a $363 million drop in commercial property values and a commercial tax rate that would rise $0.83 to $19.77.

Winter Warming Center: Members asked how neighbor concerns would be handled. Staff said flyers with contact information would go to nearby abutters, and that changes were made after last year's review.
Air rifle rodent control: Members asked whether police had weighed in. Staff said the company would coordinate with police and the city director.
Accessory dwelling unit zoning: Sponsors said the change needs more discussion, so it went back to the Land Use Committee.
